summary: A good, realistic paper. Parts 1-3 have the self-corrections and rejected options of the real test, and all keys are correct. One distractor in the Part 2 box was true of every walk, which could confuse students, and has been replaced. Part 4 is slightly easy because its notes follow the lecture almost word for word.
strengths: Part 1 corrections are natural and frequent (Sunday -> Saturday, 10 -> 11 o'clock, 25 -> 28 thousand, 17th -> 24th March, CV vs reference).
Part 2 MCQs each name all three options and rule two out (single meeting point, evening walks; library, website; footpaths, map).
Part 3 is a lively two-student discussion in which every rejected option is raised and argued away.
Part 4 is a clear, well-organised academic lecture of good length (about 700 words).

issues.problem: Box option B 'must be booked in advance' was true of every walk (the organiser says to book any walk at the tourist office), so a student could defensibly pick it for any of Q15-20.
issues.change: Replaced option B with 'offers reduced prices for children', which is not true of any walk. No answer key uses B, so no key changed.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes repeat the lecture's wording almost exactly (e.g. 'instruments called ___', 'known as ___', 'has become ___'), so Part 4 is easier than a typical real Part 4 and offers little paraphrase.
issues.change: Reword the notes (not the script), e.g. Q31 'recorded by ___ placed on the slopes', Q37 'a drop in gas output can signal a ___ vent', Q40 'data analysed together at an ___'.
